headline: Postgres rewritten in Rust now passing 100% of the Postgres regression tests
summary: The pgrust project achieves full compatibility with Postgres 18.3, matching expected output across over 46,000 regression queries and booting from existing data directories.
details: pgrust, a rewrite of Postgres in Rust, has successfully passed 100% of the Postgres regression tests. It targets compatibility with Postgres 18.3 and matches expected output across more than 46,000 regression queries.

The project is disk compatible with Postgres and can boot from an existing Postgres 18.3 data directory. The primary goal is to simplify internal modifications to Postgres, leveraging Rust and AI-assisted programming.

Currently, pgrust is not production-ready or performance optimized. Existing Postgres extensions and procedural language extensions like PL/Python are not yet generally compatible, though some bundled contrib modules have been ported.
The latest implementation has reached this significant regression-test milestone. Developers are encouraged to open issues for setup confusion, breaks, or desired Postgres improvements.

headline_marked: [[Google Home gets AI automation suggestions]] in latest biweekly update
headline: Google Home gets AI automation suggestions in latest biweekly update
summary: Google Home and Gemini for Home receive a biweekly update, introducing AI-powered automation suggestions for common tasks and a refreshed visual design for Gemini on smart displays.
details: Google is rolling out a new biweekly update for Google Home and Gemini for Home, bringing a mix of new features and improvements. The most notable addition is AI-powered automation suggestions in the Google Home app, designed to simplify smart home setup.
Gemini for Home also receives a refreshed visual design for weather forecasts and general knowledge queries on smart displays. This aims to make responses more appealing and user-friendly.

Additionally, Gemini for Home now offers more reliable and accurate sports updates, including scores, schedules, and highlights. Continued Conversation has also been improved for more reliable follow-up questions.

The new Suggested automations feature will appear at the top of the Automations tab or below existing scheduled automations. These ready-made routines cover tasks like home security, morning routines, and energy savings, rolling out to all users in the coming weeks.
For compatible cameras, the Google Home app now includes a light button directly in the camera view. Users can easily toggle the light on/off and long-press to adjust brightness.

These improvements, along with various bug fixes, are part of Google's consistent updates since the Gemini for Home Early Access program launched last October. Users can expect to see these changes appear on their devices over the coming weeks.
